extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO; counsel and Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO Final Order resolving disciplinary charges against a registered patent attorney, stating stipulated facts, legal conclusions (violations of USPTO disciplinary rules), and agreed sanctions and procedures for enforcement and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction under statute and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the Office's authority to approve settlement agreements and impose discipline; the Final Order cites these authorities as the basis for the proceeding and the approval of the Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition against neglecting client matters, illustrated here by not providing a client with accurate information about the status of a patent application and by not timely filing a change of correspondence address after withdrawing from representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the Order: representing to a client that an application had been filed when it had not; keeping oneself as correspondence address after terminating representation and failing to file a change so the client would not receive Office correspondence (e.g., a request for reexamination). Such conduct is deemed neglect under § 10.77(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(4) — prompt delivery of client property
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to promptly deliver to a client property in the practitioner's possession that the client is entitled to receive (e.g., the client's application file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order example: failing to transfer a client's file until seven weeks after request constitutes a violation. The practitioner acknowledged the client was entitled to reimbursement for expenses resulting from the practitioner's failure to file and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand as an available sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may be publicly reprimanded for violations of the USPTO disciplinary rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement/orders may include a public reprimand to be published in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette, with a Notice of Reprimand and Probation describing the violations and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation conditions and enforcement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement on an eighteen-month probationary period (commencing on date of reinstatement petition grant), with specific enforcement steps if the OED DGC believes the practitioner failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OED DGC believes noncompliance: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause, (B) send it to the practitioner's last address of record, and (C) grant 15 days to respond. If OED DGC remains of the opinion noncompliance occurred, it will deliver the Order to Show Cause, the practitioner's response (if any), and evidence/argument to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to eighteen months for the specified violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution/payment obligations and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner required to pay restitution to an affected client in a specified amount and according to a specified schedule (here, $1,350 to Brian G.: $500 by Jan 1, 2012; $500 by Mar 1, 2012; $350 by May 1, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must provide, within fifteen days of each payment due date, an affidavit and corroborating document(s) (e.g., copy of payment letter, copy of check mailed) demonstrating compliance. Returned checks for insufficient funds or late payments constitute violations of the Agreement and Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to provide timely affidavits and corroborating documents demonstrating compliance with payment and notice obligations in the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: within 15 days of each restitution payment due date submit affidavit and corroborating documents; within 30 days of the Final Order provide a copy of the Order to the person to whom payments are to be paid and within 45 days provide affidavit and corroborating docs (e.g., copy of letter mailed) demonstrating compliance with that notice requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for returned checks or late payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any check issued in payment that is returned for insufficient funds or any payment made after its due date will be deemed a violation of the Agreement and Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such violations can trigger the enforcement procedures specified for probationary noncompliance, including Order to Show Cause and possible suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED DGC shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the required Notice of Reprimand and Probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published notice must identify the practitioner, the regulations violated (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.77(c) and 10.112(c)(4)), a brief description of the misconduct, and the sanctions (reprimand, probation, restitution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO customer numbers and PKI upon suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended pursuant to the Order to Show Cause/probation enforcement, the USPTO will dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates, and the practitioner may not use or obtain such customer numbers or PKI certificates unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an immediate administrative consequence of suspension to prevent continued access to USPTO electronic services during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to dismiss pending disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: OED DGC shall file a motion to dismiss any disciplinary proceeding currently pending against the practitioner within thirty days of the Final Order being signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural step tied to settlement; it does not preclude the Office from seeking further discipline for the same misconduct in other procedural contexts described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of Office's right to seek further discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against the practitioner under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57 for misconduct that caused suspension, and nothing prevents the Office from considering this record in future proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly permits the Office to use the record (including this Final Order) (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct; and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements on the practitioner's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement obligations and regulatory references
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order does not alter the practitioner's obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 in connection with any current suspension, nor the showings required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 when seeking reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition for reinstatement must satisfy the regulatory requirements; probation commences upon grant of a reinstatement petition as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED DGC and the practitioner shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement specifies each party pays its own costs; this is part of the agreed resolution.
